summary: Appends a node to the tail of a doubly linked list. Head pointer lives at this+0x100 (this[64]); node links are prev at node+0x100 and next at node+0x104. If the list is non-empty it walks from the head to the tail via next pointers, then links the new node after the old tail (old tail next = a2, a2 prev = old tail, a2 next = 0). If the list is empty it sets the head to a2 and zeroes both new-node links. Returns the previous head (or the new node when the list was empty).

operations.description: Read head pointer this[64] at offset 0x100; if null the list is empty and the new node becomes the head.
Walk from the head following next pointers at node+0x104 until the tail (node whose next is null) is reached.
Non-empty path: set old tail's next (+0x104) to a2, set a2's prev (+0x100) to the old tail, and set a2's next (+0x104) to 0.
Empty path: set head this[64] (offset 0x100) to a2, then set a2's prev (+0x100) and next (+0x104) both to 0.
Return the previous head pointer, or the new node when the list was empty.
